item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning yes on programmatic expansion of basic services, but access was uneven and conflict-driven disruption kept 2024 from being a clean welfare-improvement year. The strongest positive evidence is in WASH, education, health-financing, food-security/safety-net, and refugee/IDP support; the strongest negative evidence is in food-aid diversion, attacks on health care, refugee water gaps, and funding shortfalls.

**Positive Evidence**
- **Breaking Barriers: Empowering Girls with Clean Water and Sanitation Facilities in Ethiopia's Schools** | World Bank | 2024-01-19 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/01/19/breaking-barriers-empowering-girls-with-clean-water-and-sanitation-facilities-in-ethiopias-schools | The program says over 5,000 schools were equipped with WASH facilities and 223 menstrual-hygiene rooms, improving attendance especially for girls. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **Ethiopia signs 1.72 billion USD Financing Agreements with the World Bank** | Ministry of Finance, Ethiopia | 2024-04-05 | https://www.mofed.gov.et/blog/ethiopia-signs-172-billion-usd-financing-agreements-with-the-world-bank/ | The financing package funded rural connectivity, adaptive safety nets, food security, and other public-good projects aimed at inclusive growth. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `5B.10`
- **Bringing Back More Schools, Health Facilities & Life in Tigray** | United Nations in Ethiopia | 2024-02-23 | https://ethiopia.un.org/en/261479-bringing-back-more-schools-health-facilities-life-tigray | The project reconstructed 14 health centers, 11 schools, and 33 WASH facilities for 365,000 people in five woredas. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **Second Phase of PROSPECTS Launched in Ethiopia, Empowering Refugees, IDPs and Host Communities** | UNICEF Ethiopia | 2024-03-21 | https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/press-releases/second-phase-prospects-launched-ethiopia-empowering-refugees-idps-and-host | The partnership targeted education, livelihoods, protection, and infrastructure for refugees, IDPs, and host communities. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **Building a Strong Foundation to Improve Learning Outcomes in Ethiopia** | World Bank | 2024-09-05 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2024/09/05/building-a-strong-foundation-to-improve-learning-outcomes-in-afe-ethiopia | The program trained 102,117 teachers and reported improved girls’ enrollment and refugee-school support in disadvantaged regions. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`
- **Ethiopia’s health-financing progress / six-year health-financing program completed** | ENA English | 2024-10-03 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5233579 | The ministry said health insurance coverage improved and financial barriers to primary care were reduced. | `6B.2`, `5B.10`
- **Ethiopia Considers Social Protection as Core Component of National Dev’t: Minister** | ENA English | 2024-11-13 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5452428 | Social protection was described as remaining central to policy, indicating explicit priority for vulnerable households. | `6B.2`
- **Social Welfare Key Pillar of Prime Ministerial Initiatives** | ENA English | 2024-08-05 | https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_4920073 | The PM office described housing support for the elderly and economically vulnerable as an ongoing initiative. This is weaker than outcome evidence, but it is direct welfare-oriented policy rhetoric. | `6B.2`

**Negative Evidence**
- **World Report 2024: Ethiopia** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-12 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/ethiopia | HRW reported aid diversion that led WFP and USAID to halt food aid, sharply restricting access for about 20 million people. | `6B.2`, `5B.8`, `5B.9`
- **UNHCR Ethiopia | WASH – Gap Analysis for Refugees | March 2024** | UNHCR | 2024-03-21 | https://data.unhcr.org/en/documents/details/107435 | Refugees were receiving about 14 liters of water per person per day, below the 20-liter minimum standard, showing incomplete WASH access. | `6B.2`
- **Ethiopia: Army Attacks Health Care in Amhara Conflict** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-03 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/03/ethiopia-army-attacks-health-care-amhara-conflict | Security forces attacked ambulances, hospitals, and medical staff, interfering with access to health care and humanitarian assistance. | `6B.2`, `5B.9`
- **Nearly 1 million refugees in Ethiopia risk limited assistance due unprecedented funding crisis** | UNHCR Africa | 2024-04-15 | https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/nearly-1-million-refugees-ethiopia-risk-limited-assistance-due-unprecedented | UNHCR warned that healthcare, education, and water gaps were directly affecting refugee lives, with assistance at risk from funding shortfalls. | `6B.2`
- **Ethiopia: Mass arbitrary detentions in Amhara region deepen erosion of rule of law** | Amnesty International | 2024-10-01 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/10/ethiopia-mass-arbitrary-detentions-in-amhara-region-deepen-erosion-of-rule-of-law/ | Mass arbitrary detentions under emergency rule show a coercive environment that undercuts welfare delivery and civilian security. | `6B.2`, `5B.9`

**Search Gap**
- I found strong direct evidence for education, WASH, food security, social protection, and health-financing improvements.
- Direct national-level evidence on ordinary housing access is thin; the strongest item I found is welfare/housing rhetoric for vulnerable people rather than a measurable housing-access outcome.
- The most serious counterevidence is not that welfare programs were absent, but that conflict, displacement, aid diversion, and emergency repression prevented access from being broad, stable, and equal.
